text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- In the last six years the European Fund for Agricultural Development provided five thousand preferential credits to modernise and develop Poland's farming and food processing industry sector worth 115 million zlotys, the Fund said.

- Poland's Huta Katowice steel plant and Belgium's Sidmar steel concern have given up a joint venture to construct a continuous casting line at the Katowice plant. The companies did not disclose reasons for the change of plans.

- Asea Brown Boveri (ABB) will acquire a 60 percent stake in the Elbud Krakow energy construction firm from the Octava National Investment Fund (NFI)-8, which holds a 33 percent stake, and the remaining 27 percent from the other funds, ABB said.

- The European Union will give up anti-dumping and anti-subsidy proceedings against associated states in central and eastern Europe, when the countries adapt the EU regulations on competition and state subsidizing, the EU Commissioner Leon Brittan said on Monday.
NOWA EUROPA
- PepsiCo Inc. is not planning to sell its shares in the listed Wedel confectionery maker, PepsiCo Central Europe regional deputy director Zbigniew Wrobel said.
- The Piast National Investment Fund (NFI)-12 will acquire a 10 percent stake in the listed Prochnik garment maker from the receiver of the bankrupt Westa insurance company.
- Agora-Gazeta, the Gazeta Wyborcza daily publisher, is planning to buy land in the Katowice Special Economic Zone to construct a computerised printing press in southern Poland.

- The listed Elektrim industrial and trading conglomerate has proposed to create a consortium with a group of banks, which will take over 51 percent stakes in four power plants to be privatised in the future, Elektrim said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Korea's Daewoo automaker sold 38,000 vehicles in Poland last year which made the country Daewoo's biggest market in Europe.
- Poland's duty free import quota for the EU-made cars will reach 38,750 cars in 1997, the economy ministry said.
ZYCIE
- PKO BP bank will increase interest on three-month deposits from 15.5 to 16 percent as of February 4, the bank said.
- KGHM copper conglomerate denied reports it was planning to shed 8,000 jobs. The information on planned redundancies has been published in a report by the provincial governor office.
PARKIET
- The Ostrow Wielkopolski Municipality is s issuing 750 000 bonds, nominally worth 10 zlotys each, and plans to introduce the securities on the CTO over-the-counter market, the municipality said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
